speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings. To understand what is happening, was the pain constant or intermittent, and did it start immediately after your surgery or much later?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: The shooting pain you describe when eating, combined with your history of chronic ear infections and recent tympanoplasty, sounds very much like Frey's syndrome (gustatory sweating). Do you also notice sweating or a warm, tingling sensation in that ear while you are eating?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Frey's Syndrome (Gustatory Sweating). The shooting ear pain triggered by eating, despite the hearing improvement and lack of reported sweating or warmth in your description, is the hallmark sign of this condition where aberrant regeneration of parasympathetic nerve fibers occurs following your tympanoplasty. While the earring discomfort may be due to a persistent tympanic membrane perforation or a small granulation tissue at the graft site, the primary issue driving your symptoms is the nerve misdirection. I have reached the diagnosis limit and will not ask further questions; if you need confirmation, a specialized test like a Minor's test or a sweat test would be required.
